open-question.question: The batched call gets an automated test under both interpreters. Is the compact view's fixed shell call, the list call followed by the walk-fed loop of lift calls, exercised by an automated test too, or does it stay covered by the Claude Code hands-on check alone?
open-question.recommendation: The call is the sweep's whole gather and the read the field broke most, so its print is pinned on every push and a regression reports as the gather's own failure, under bash to match the decided batched-call test and with no git setup since the call writes nothing; the anchor the sibling settles finds this second fence by a command only it carries, list with its question flag.
open-question.alternative: An automated test of its own in tests/, run in CI under both pytest interpreters, that extracts the compact view call from a rendered host tree, replaces <MILESTONE_DIR> with a golden fixture milestone copied to a temporary directory, runs the call under bash, and asserts its print: every block's id, tab, and question text in document order, recommendation-less blocks included, followed by each walked id and that id's lifted line in walk order. Bash only, matching the batched-call test; no git repository is needed since the call writes nothing. The read the sweep reasons over is pinned on every push, independently of the batched-call test, so a regression in the gather is reported as the gather's failure, and the test is cheap because the call has no per-question placeholder to fill and needs no git setup. Bash is not the shell that broke the field reads (zsh), so the test does not reach the failure class that motivated the compact view, and the failed-lift branch (an Error: line in place of the pick) cannot be provoked from a valid fixture, since walk prints only blocks lift accepts, so that branch stays with the hands-on check. Depends on the extraction anchor the sibling question settles also locating a second fixed call in the same rendered file.

No automated test of the compact view call, for good unless a later field run shows it breaking: the call stays covered by the Claude Code hands-on check of the rewritten sweep, and its three tool calls stay covered by the existing per-subcommand suites (test_list.py, test_walk.py, test_lift.py). No new test, fixture, or extraction anchor is added for it, and the batched-call test is the milestone's only template test. The call adds no logic of its own beyond running list, then walk's ids through a read loop into lift, and every one of those prints is already pinned by the tool's tests, so the only untested part is a few lines of shell glue that the hands-on check runs for real, in the user's own shell, at no added test or anchor cost. The call is the sweep's whole gather and order and the read that the field broke most often (33 of 88 runs lost a turn to the zsh separator in today's read), yet a later edit that breaks it, drops the list half, or reorders its print passes CI and surfaces only in a run or in the next hands-on check, which today covers no host's sweep at all.

alternative.id: Separate executed test under bash and zsh

open-question.alternative: The same separate executed test as under bash, extracting the call from a rendered host tree, running it on a copied fixture milestone, and asserting the same print, but run once under bash and once under zsh, the zsh run skipping itself where no zsh is installed, in CI under both pytest interpreters. It exercises the call in the shell that broke today's read (the macOS default, where the separator's =cmd expansion failed), so a later edit that reintroduces a zsh-unsafe form fails a test on any maintainer machine that has zsh rather than in a field run. CI's ubuntu-latest runner is not guaranteed to carry zsh, so the zsh leg may run only on maintainer machines and skip silently in CI, adding an environment-keyed skip to a suite whose only skip today is keyed on the interpreter version; the failed-lift branch stays unprovokable from a valid fixture, and it depends on the sibling's extraction anchor also locating a second call.

No separate test: the batched-call test already decided gains a first stage that extracts the compact view call from the same rendered host tree, runs it under bash on the same fixture milestone in its temporary git repository, asserts its print, and fills each batched section's --option value and expected commit body from the lifted lines that print carries rather than from fixture constants, so the two calls are exercised as one run in CI under both pytest interpreters. It covers the hand-off the Option value source decision describes, the runner copying each section's option from the compact view's lifted pick, so a drift between what the compact view prints and what the batched call needs fails one end-to-end test, with one fixture and one harness and no second test file. A compact view regression fails the batched-call test, so a failure no longer says which call broke, and the batched test's correctness now rests on a gather it does not control; it runs under bash only, the failed-lift branch stays unprovokable, and it depends on the sibling's extraction anchor locating both calls in the one rendered file.

alternative.id: Static assertion on the rendered call

open-question.alternative: An automated test in tests/, run in CI under both pytest interpreters, that reads the compact view call from a rendered host tree without running it and asserts its text: list --with-question, walk, and lift each written as the full fixed tool command with no variable, alias, or function standing for it, the loop reading walk's print, and no echo separator between reads. No fixture is copied and no shell runs. It guards exactly the regressions the field and the shell-literal invariant name (a separator, a shortened tool command) at the lowest harness cost of any test, with no fixture, temporary directory, or shell dependency. It checks the file rather than the run, so a call that is textually right but prints the wrong shape or order passes, the field failures came from runners rewriting commands, which no test of the file reaches, and it starts a new kind of test, prose assertions on a rendered skill, that the suite does not hold today; it depends on the sibling's extraction anchor also locating this call.

open-question.question: The compact view gives the sweep each walked question's id, question text, and lifted pick, that is the option id and the recommendation's one-line rationale, and the whole XML is no longer read, while today's folds draw the recorded decision's detail from the picked alternative's what-it-is text. Is each sweep decision written from the lifted line alone, or does the compact view also carry the picked alternative's what-it-is text for every walked id?
open-question.recommendation: A recorded decision needs the picked option's positions, which the option label and one-line rationale do not carry and which today's folds take from the located block, so the view fetches each walked pick's what-it-is inside the one decided call, at no extra turn and with no per-pick judgment, while still leaving out every unpicked alternative, advantage, and drawback; the shell split it adds is pinned by the compact view's own executed test.
open-question.alternative: The compact view's fixed call is extended, still one call with no tool change. Inside its walk-fed loop, after printing each id and its lift line, it takes the option id from that line in the shell (the text before the first spaced em dash, by parameter expansion on the held line), runs lift --alternative with it, and prints that alternative's what-it-is line beneath. A walked id whose lift fails prints its Error: line and no alternative line. Every walked id with a pick gets its what-it-is, and each decision is written from the question text, the lifted line, and that what-it-is. The remove --option value is still the runner's literal copy of the option. Every sweep decision keeps the detail today's folds draw from the located block, the concrete positions that the option id and the rationale's reasons leave out. It costs no extra turn and needs no judgment about which picks need it. The view still leaves out the unpicked alternatives and every advantage and drawback, so it stays far smaller than the XML. The fixed call gains a second per-item shell value and a shell-side split of the lifted line. That is the same first-spaced-em-dash split the lift procedure defines for RECORDED OPTION, now done in the shell and used only for display, and the shell-literal clause for the sweep must cover the extra value too. The view also grows by one what-it-is per walked block, text with no length limit, which narrows the measured 9–13× saving over the XML. Whether this added shell logic is caught by anything besides the hands-on check depends on the axis the Compact view test coverage question owns.

The compact view stays exactly as decided: list --with-question, then each walked id with its lift line. Nothing else about the question document is fetched. Each sweep decision is written from the block's question text, the option id, and the recommendation's one-line rationale alone, at the detail those carry. No lift --alternative, locate, or other read of the picked alternative happens at any point in the run. The view, its one fixed call, and the setup turn count stay exactly as the Compact view command decision fixed them, with no extra value, parse, or call. The decision is drawn only from the line that also becomes the commit body, so the recorded text and the commit record say the same thing. The option id is a short label and the rationale states reasons rather than positions. The concrete content of the pick, which today's folds take from the what-it-is (the stop-report decision's silenced lift stderr and fixed stopped-at line, for instance), is either left out or rebuilt by the runner from the label and the question text, which is the invented answer text the lift procedure forbids. Sweep decisions then carry less than the hand-answer skills' decisions, which keep their locate, while `## Decisions` is what derive-tasks and later reviews read.

The compact view's call stays exactly as decided. After reading its print, the runner composes and runs a second call. It holds one lift --alternative per walked id whose lift succeeded, each with the block's Short Title and the option id copied literally from the compact view's lift line, and each invocation written as the full fixed command. The runner reads its print before composing the batched call. Every walked pick gets its what-it-is, and each decision is written from the question text, the lifted line, and that what-it-is. Every decision gets the full detail while the compact view's fixed call and its decided shape stay untouched. The option reaches lift --alternative as an exact id the runner copied, the same discipline the batched call keeps for remove --option, with no shell-side parse of the answer text. Every run that walks a pick pays one more setup turn, which must come after the compact view because the ids come from its print. That works against the goal of collapsing the setup to its fixed-call floor. The second call is composed per run rather than fixed and run as shown, so it is one more runner-written template beside the batched call, and the context grows by the same what-it-is text as carrying it in the view.

The compact view's call stays exactly as decided, and each decision is written from the question text and the lifted line by default. When the runner judges that a pick's question text, option id, and rationale do not state concretely enough what was decided, it fetches the what-it-is of those picks only. It does so before composing the batched call, in one call of lift --alternative lines with the option ids copied literally. A run whose lifted lines all suffice fetches nothing. A run pays for the alternative text only where the lifted line falls short. Runs whose rationales already name the decided positions keep the decided view and turn count, and thin picks still get their detail. It adds a per-pick judgment to a sweep otherwise made a pure recorder of picks as given, and the setup no longer has a fixed call count. A miss is silent: a thin decision is folded and committed with nothing flagging it. Option ids are short labels and the rationale is written as brief reasons, so many picks are likely to need the fetch, and the option then tends to cost what the separate call costs plus the judgment.

The compact view stays as decided, and each decision is written from the question text and the lifted line alone, with no what-it-is fetched by the sweep. In addition, the recommendation pass's rendering and recommend-procedure.md are changed so that the one-line rationale states the picked option's concrete positions as well as why it was picked. That makes the lifted line enough for the fold on its own. The sweep's view and calls stay minimal, with no parse and no extra turn. The one line the sweep reads, which is also the commit body that capture walks, carries the decision's substance, so the commit body alone tells what was decided. It widens the milestone to the recommendation pass and its procedure, which the goal does not name. Picks already standing, in this milestone and in other projects, were formed under the brief-rationale rule and stay thin until they are re-picked. The rationale stops being a brief reason and restates the what-it-is in a second place, which lengthens every pick and every Recommendation-answer body that capture reads as evidence.
